copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Survives a Dead Receiver Room
copies.body:
CJ started two wide receivers and got 2.0 points out of them. Rashee Rice posted a zero on a 14.9 projection, Parker Washington managed 2.0 on 15.3, and CJ still won, because the running backs refused to let it matter. Jonathan Taylor 22.7, Chuba Hubbard 25.9, Quinshon Judkins 21.6 out of the flex — 70.2 from three backs against Noah's 34.7 at the position. That 13.9-point RB edge, plus the flex, was the entire margin and then some.
Noah lost this the way he's lost all four: nothing broke wrong, nothing broke right either. Garrett Wilson and Josh Downs combined for 10.3 on 30.1 of projection, and Drake Maye put up 26.2 on the bench while Patrick Mahomes gave him 17.0. Start the kid you named the team after.
CJ is 3-1 with an all-play of 24-20, which says he's fine, not scary. Noah is 0-4, last in scoring, last in all-play at 7-37 — and he's still the guy nobody wants to see in January.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Backfield Buries Grant By Five
copies.body:
The running backs decided this. Ashton Jeanty and RJ Harvey combined for 37.9 while Grant got 20.3 out of Omarion Hampton and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, a 17.6-point gap that Grant's receivers nearly erased on their own — Zay Flowers went for 25.8 and Amon-Ra St. Brown added 15.5, a 18.9-point edge at wideout. Jared Goff's 20.5 against Kyler Murray's 11.5 was the quiet closer. Murray was projected for 19.2. That shortfall alone is bigger than the margin.
Kaleb won this with a zero in his lineup. Ladd McConkey posted 0.0 on an 11.7 projection while Carnell Tate hung 21.5 on the bench, which should have been fatal. It wasn't, because Grant was busy leaving his own points behind: Jaylen Waddle's 14.5 rotting while Christian Watson delivered 7.7, and Tony Pollard's 13.0 behind Croskey-Merritt's 7.0.
We picked Grant by nine, which looks dumber than it was. He's 2-2 with a 16-28 all-play, 10th in the league. Kaleb is 3-1, 7th in all-play, and already banking the luck that keeps 8-6 seasons alive.

copies.headline: Kincaid Sinks Isaac While Hockenson Watches
copies.body:
This one was decided at tight end and kicker, which is a humiliating sentence to write. Dalton Kincaid put up 1.7 on a 10.7 projection while T.J. Hockenson scored 24.9 from Isaac's bench — a 23-point swing that, by itself, nearly covers John's 25.4 margin. Add Chris Boswell's 3.1 against Cam Little's 14.7 and the Lions defense going negative, and Isaac lost this game in the spots nobody wants to think about on Sunday morning.
The skill positions were close to a wash. Javonte Williams went for 31.3, Malik Nabers added 23.2, and C.J. Stroud outscored Matthew Stafford by 13.4. But Ja'Marr Chase managed 5.7 on a 20.4 projection with DK Metcalf and his 16.5 sitting right there, and Cam Skattebo missed by 8.5. John just needed Kyren Williams (36.7) and Puka Nacua (27.7) to show up, and they did.
We had John by 11; he got 25.4. Isaac falls to 2-2 with an all-play of 13-31 that says he's been fortunate to be this close to .500 at all.

copies.headline: Adam's Running Backs Bury Mitchell's Backfield
copies.body:
Mitchell lost this at running back, and it wasn't close. Kenneth Walker III alone put up 30.9, more than Mitchell's entire RB room, which managed 20.7 between Jahmyr Gibbs (17.7 on a 26.1 projection) and George Holani's 3.0. Sam LaPorta added 22.4 at tight end against Tyler Warren's 9.1, and then Will Reichard kicked 20.0 to Tyler Loop's 8.4, which is the kind of indignity you can't game-plan around. Adam won four of seven positions and the three he won big accounted for 41.2 points of a 44.3-point margin.
Nico Collins' 30.8 was wasted, because DJ Moore gave back 2.7 on a 13.0 projection and the Bills defense contributed 1.0. Mitchell has now scored 73.0, 149.2 and 102.5 in three weeks — the human coin flip, landing on its edge. Our preview had Adam by 21; we were too conservative.
Adam is 4-0 with a 40-4 all-play, 152.7 a game, first in the league in both. The reigning champ isn't sneaking up on anyone. Mitchell drops to 1-3 and the math is getting unfriendly.

copies.headline: Peter's Receivers Erased Leif Before Halftime
copies.body:
The wideout room did it. Peter got 50.5 from Tee Higgins and Romeo Doubs; Leif got 15.7 from Davante Adams and Stefon Diggs combined, a 34.8-point hole no quarterback play was going to patch, and the quarterbacks were effectively tied anyway. Add Tucker Kraft's 16.5 against Dalton Schultz's 2.9 and Kyle Monangai's 28.0 off the Chicago backfield lottery, and Peter won six of seven positions on his way to 163.0, his season high by 37.
Leif's 82.8 is a season low and it wasn't close to bad luck. Adams missed his projection by 8.4, Schultz by 6.1, David Montgomery by 9.2, and Mike Evans sat on the bench with 12.6 while Montgomery flexed into 4.3. Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry all showed up and it bought him nothing. We picked Leif by 16, which aged like milk.
Peter is 4-0 with a +1.5 luck figure, so the scoring doesn't entirely back the record — but a 61% all-play says he isn't a fraud either. Leif is 2-2, losers of two, and Joey Lunchbox is drifting toward his natural habitat.

copies.headline: Logan's backfield no-shows, Christian cruises again
copies.body:
The running backs decided this before either receiver room got going. Christian got 35.9 from Chase Brown and Aaron Jones Sr.; Logan got 8.5 from Saquon Barkley and Jeremiyah Love combined, a 27.4-point hole he was never climbing out of. Barkley put up 2.0 against a 14.3 projection, Love 6.5 against 15.6, and Emanuel Wilson sat on the bench scoring 27.0. Even the kickers piled on — Brandon Aubrey 10.9, Chase McLaughlin 2.0.
The wide receivers essentially canceled out. Tetairoa McMillan's 45.2 was the best individual line in the matchup, and it bought Logan nothing because CeeDee Lamb answered with 41.3 and Christian's WR room still won the position. We picked Christian by 21 and he beat that by half again, even leaving Alvin Kamara's 22.8 on the bench behind Bhayshul Tuten's 11.1.
Christian's 1-3 is a lie — 134.7 per game, second in the league, 29-15 all-play, and 1.6 wins of bad luck. Logan is 0-4 at 104.8 a week, and the all-play says he's earned most of it. The dress is already measuring him.

intro: Peter's 162.98 was the week's high score and it landed on Leif's 82.82, an 80-point gap that qualifies less as a matchup than as a crime scene. Christian and Adam both cleared 146 to bury Logan and Mitchell, while the only competitive football happened at the top of the board — CJ survived Noah by 4.1 and Kaleb edged Grant by 5.2. Four of six games were decided by 25 or more, so if you lost this week, you probably lost it on Thursday.
